ON THE 4 th OF DECEMBER, 2025  MISC. APPEAL No. 359 of 2018  NAHARU @ NAHARULAL  Versus  DILIP AND OTHERS  Appearance:
 Shri Anand Bhatt, learned counsel for the appellant.

sentences.text: Ms. Priya Sharma, learned counsel for the respondent  Shri Manoj Jain, learned counsel for the respondent   ORDER

The appellant/claimant has filed this appeal under Section 173 of Motor Vehicles Act being aggrieved by the award dated 30.6.2017 passed in Claims Case No.80/2015, whereby challenging quantum of compensation on the ground that income has not been assessed properly.

2. Short facts of the case are that on 19.4.2015 at around 12.30 in the afternoon appellant Nahru @
Nahrulal, aged 30 years, was going on a motorcycle with other two persons from Daulatpura to Sailana.
Appellant Nahru was riding the same and two other persons were sitting as pillion riders.

When they reached in front of I.T.I., Kariya Road, Sailana, Maruti Van No.RJ-27-UB-5842 came,
which was being driven by respondent No.1 in a rash and negligent manner dashed into the motorcycle of Nahru.
Because of which all three of them suffered grievous injuries.
Appellant suffered NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:35460 2 MA-359-2018 fracture of his clavicle and scapula bone of right shoulder and tibia fibula bone and right lower limb.

The appellant was subjected to the medical examination by District Medical Board, Ratlam, which certified the permanent disability of the appellant at 55% vide certificate Ex.P/104.
2.1
The appellant filed claim petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act claiming compensation for the injuries sustained by the appellant in the aforesaid accident.
The claims Tribunal after recording evidence concluded that the insured vehicle was at fault in as much as the said vehicle was driven in rash and negligent manner, which caused the accident.
hence, a total compensation of Rs.3,73,600/- was awarded to the appellant while considering his loss of earning capacity at 55%.

3. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that although the extent of permanent disability has Naharu @ Naharulal vs Dilip on 4 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/68989797/
1 correctly been assessed, however, the income has been taken only at Rs.3,000/- per month on notional basis, which is not correct.

He points out that the income should have been taken at least Rs.15,000/- per month as he was working as Mason before his accident and he has suffered complete paralysis of right hand and permanent disability into right lower limb.
He is not able to continue his work.
As such, the compensation should be enhanced as regards loss of earning capacity.
He further submits that meager amount of Rs.5,000/- has been awarded for pain and suffering and Rs.7,000/- for special died, which should also be enhanced accordingly.

4. On the other hand, learned counsel for the respondent/Insurance company supports the findings of the award and points out that 55% NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:35460 3 MA-359-2018 permanent disability has been assigned by the Medical Board with respect to right lower limb and left lower limb and not with respect to whole body considering that there are four limbs in the body, it should have been taken at 26% hence the claims Tribunal has not assessed the loss of earning capacity correctly.

He further submits that perusal of the findings recorded by the Tribunal regarding income of the appellant and the record of the Tribunal would show that there was complete absence of any material to establish that appellant was working as Mason, the Tribunal has not committed any illegality in assessing income at Rs.3,000/- per month.
He, thus prays for dismissal of the appeal.

5. Heard learned counsel for the parties; perused the record.
6.

A perusal of Ex.P/104 issued by the District Medical Board, Ratlam would show that after considering the fact that appellant sustained fracture of right upper limb has certified the same at 55% with respect to those two parts of the body.

However, it has to be taken into account that there is specific statement of medical expert with respect to the nature of permanent disability suffered by the appellant, his right upper limb has rendered completely paralysed.
As such, contention of learned counsel for the Insurance Company that the overall permanent disability should be taken at 26% cannot be countenanced.
Considering the nature of injuries suffered by the appellant overall loss of earning capacity is taken at 50%.
Considering the fact that accident occurred in the year 2015 the notional income of Rs.3,000/- per month is appears to be on lower side.
Thus, the same is hereby revised to Rs.5,000/- per month.

Considering the law as laid down by the Hon'ble Apex NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:35460 4 MA-359-2018 Court in the case of National Insurance Co.Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi , reported in 2017 ACJ 2700 , 40% addition is made in the said income under the head of future prospects considering the age of appellant at 30 years at the time of accident.

sentences.text: 7. As such, the amount of compensation for loss of earning capacity would now come to Rs.7,14,000/-.
Considering that only an amount of Rs.5,000/- has been awarded for pain and suffering and Rs.7,000/- for special diet, further addition of Rs.25,000/- is made in the same head.

After including the other amounts as awarded by the Tribunal total compensation would now come to Rs.7,76,000/- and after deducting the already awarded amount of Rs.3,73,600/-, the appellant is now entitled for payment of Rs.4,02,400/- over and above the amount already awarded by the claims Tribunal with an interest @ 6% per annum from the date of filing of claim application till its payment.
